I1.quote: Searched the main text (all 5 pages; no supplementary file was supplied) for an H2 uptake the authors measured themselves by a gravimetric, volumetric (Sieverts) or flow method, or any experimental section, instrument or sample. None found: every uptake value (Table 3) is from molecular dynamics simulation, and experimental work is only cited from refs [1-3], [30].

I5.quote: Physisorption of molecular hydrogen on pristine single-walled carbon nanotube and three types of topologically defected nanotubes (Stone-Wales, vacancy and interstitial defects) at different temperatures 77, 300 and 600 K has been investigated via molecular dynamics simulation.

notes: Pure molecular dynamics study, so I1 fails and the code is theoretical_only. Supporting quotes: "we have performed the molecular dynamics (MD) simulation on defected nanotube (three above mentioned defects) and defect-free nanotube (pristine nanotube) at different temperatures (77, 300 and 600 K)." (main, p. 2, Section 2 Computational methods); "Table 3 e Hydrogen adsorption capacities calculated at 77 K." (main, p. 4, Table 3 caption); "The calculated H2 adsorption capacities of the four nanotubes are summarized in Table 3." (main, p. 4, Section 3). The 1 bar pressure is a simulation setting ("The simulations were performed under ambient pressure of 1 bar for all the systems.", main, p. 3, Section 2). Primary research article; record.json is_retracted false and no retraction notice in the PDF; no statement that the values were published before. Page numbers are PDF pages 1-5 (journal pp. 13250-13254).
